issues.issue: "Net Eligible Revenue" is capitalised as a defined term but is defined nowhere in this Agreement, only in the extrinsic New FA Compensation Plan.

The adjustment operates through "monthly compensation under the New FA Compensation Plan", which under Paragraph 4 only begins after graduation, leaving no mechanism for a salaried New FA under Paragraph 3.

The disclosure describes arbitration of "any dispute, claim or controversy that may arise between you and Wells Fargo Advisors, or a client, or any other person", and the catch-all "any other person" has no discernible limit.

This description of the scope of arbitration is broader than the operative clause in Paragraph 14(b), which covers only controversies "arising between you and Wells Fargo Advisors", so the summary and the operative term point in different directions.

The statement that statutory discrimination claims "IS REQUIRED to be arbitrated" sits against Paragraph 14(a)(4), which preserves the right to file agency charges, and against Paragraph 14(b), which lists discrimination among arbitrable claims without the exclusions stated in 14(a)(3).

The exclusion is for "claims for State unemployment insurance", but the "i.e." list that follows includes workers' compensation and "claims under the National Labor Relations Act", which are not State unemployment insurance; the category and its illustrations do not match.

These exclusions appear only in the explanatory Paragraph 14(a), whereas the operative arbitration clause in Paragraph 14(b) says "Except as provided in Paragraph 14(c)" and carries no such carve-outs, leaving it uncertain whether the exclusions are operative.

The preservation of agency charges followed by automatic arbitration "upon receipt of a right to sue letter or similar administrative determination" is in tension with Paragraph 14(a)(3), which excludes certain administratively processed claims from arbitration altogether.
The clause reads "the rules of the arbitration forum in the claim is filed", omitting a word ("in which"), which garbles the reference to the forum whose rules govern panel composition.

The statement that "a claim that is ineligible for arbitration may be brought to court" is in tension with Paragraph 14(b)'s directive that claims FINRA does not accept go instead to the American Arbitration Association.

The clause lists specific claim types and closes with "and/or other theory", a catch-all whose reach against the enumerated specifics is uncertain, and it is limited to disputes "arising between you and Wells Fargo Advisors" without any "arising out of employment" limitation.
Paragraph 14(b) excepts only Paragraph 14(c) and so appears to compel arbitration of the very claims Paragraph 14(a)(3) says are "specifically EXCLUDED from this obligation to arbitrate".

The carve-out from arbitration runs one way only — Wells Fargo alone may seek court relief "[n]otwithstanding any other provision" — which is the kind of one-sided drafting that invites construction against the drafter.

The survival list expressly preserves "indemnification obligations", but the Agreement contains no indemnification provision — Paragraph 13 imposes only a contribution expectation — so the reference cannot be matched to any operative term.

Missouri law is chosen for an agreement made for a New York branch employee whose restrictive covenants in Paragraphs 11 and 12 would ordinarily be tested under New York law; nothing else in the instrument addresses that mismatch.

The fallback says invalidity "shall not affect the validity or unenforceability of the remaining Provisions", which as written preserves their unenforceability — plainly a drafting slip inverting the intended sense.
The clause preserves rights only as to "any other breach of the same or any other covenant", which by negative implication suggests that forbearance does waive the individual breach forgone.

The paragraph is headed "RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS" and acknowledges covenants "IN THEIR ENTIRETY", yet contains none itself and Paragraph 17 says captions "shall not affect in any way the meaning or interpretation", leaving which provisions are the acknowledged restrictive covenants unsettled.
The integration is qualified by "regarding the matters addressed herein", a limitation whose scope is itself indeterminate.

The declaration of an entire understanding cannot be squared with Paragraph 8, which says the Agreement "serves only as a synopsis", or with Paragraph 6, which says it "does not supersede or replace" Wells Fargo's human resources policies and compliance guidelines.
"All provisions ... that require survival ... in order to give full legal effect thereto" is circular: it identifies the surviving provisions only by reference to their own need to survive.
This open-ended survival rule overlaps with Paragraph 15, which already specifies which terms survive termination, leaving it unclear whether Paragraph 15's list is exhaustive.
